nodes.name: Ni65Fe35(OOH) Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The Ni–Fe(OOH) catalyst was prepared by electrodeposition on ~25 μm thick conductive graphene sheets (Graphene Supermarket) roughened with sand paper. The deposition solution constituted 9 mL of 50 mM Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (99.999% trace metals basis, Sigma-Aldrich) and 1 mL of 50 mM Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O (≥99.999% trace metals basis, Sigma-Aldrich). The catalyst films were deposited galvanostatically on a geometric area of ca. 0.4 cm² using a 2-electrode setup where a fine Pt-coil served as counter electrode. A current density of -2.5 mA cm⁻² was applied for 113 s, using a Bio-Logic SP-200 potentiostat.
nodes.source_text: Ni–Fe catalyst deposition and electrolyte preparation. The Ni–Fe(OOH) catalyst was prepared by electrodeposition... This resulted in a film with a Ni:Fe stoichiometry of 65:35 at.%

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS supports non-covalent catalyst-cation interaction with no traces of alkali cations in rinsed Ni-Fe films; shows local Ni:Fe compositional inhomogeneity with Fe-enrichment areas.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) further supports a non-covalent catalyst-cation interaction, since there were no traces of cations in the Ni–Fe films post-OER after carefully rinsing with MilliQ-water.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determined Ni:Fe stoichiometry of 65:35 at% and geometric metal loading of ~25±2 μg cm⁻² for the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This resulted in a film with a Ni:Fe stoichiometry of 65:35 at.%, and a geometric metal loading (with respect to both Ni and Fe content) of ~25±2 μg cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Ni and Fe K-edge XAS reveals Ni²⁺Fe³⁺ ground state (1.1 V) with Ni–O ~2.04 Å, Ni–Ni ~3.06 Å, Fe–O ~1.99 Å, Fe–Ni ~3.06 Å; oxidation above ~1.35 V shifts Ni to Ni^(3+δ)+ with Ni–O shortening to ~1.88 Å at 1.66 V (Ni³.⁸⁺), Fe remains mostly Fe³⁺ with minor Fe⁴⁺ (~60-90%) suggested by Fe–O ~1.94 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At non-catalytic potential... the K-edge positions match low-valent Ni²⁺Fe³⁺... Simulations of the k³-weighted EXAFS... Ni–O ~2.04 Å, Ni-Ni ~3.06 Å, Fe–O ~1.99 Å, and Fe–Ni ~3.06 Å... At 1.66 V the following average bond lengths are obtained; Ni–O (~1.88 Å), Ni–Fe (~2.82 Å), Fe–O (~1.94 Å), and Fe–Ni (~2.89 Å).
